searches.note: Twenty one searches of a share of twenty eight, seven left unspent, none of them the author's. Shared: the STK and its founding of 1986, the three Styrian DACs from the 2018 vintage (restricted to austrianwine.com), the Weststeiermark rules (austrianwine.com, steiermark.wine, ris.bka.gv.at, read as primary through their summaries), and the name Schilcher (the Austrian Ministry of Agriculture's page among the results). The house's own domain was blocked wherever a second, independent source was wanted (tement.at three times, sattlerhof.at once, gross.at three times, neumeister.cc twice, weingut-langmann.at twice). No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and the rules, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail rested on one non primary source it was hedged, cut or said with less.
Sources whose title or address names a living person, and result summaries carrying prices and scores, were met and are cited neither in the fragment nor here.

story: was he who planted the Kranachberg, a site many growers share (wein.plus lists seven); now he planted the family's vines there, as it tells it; was Falstaff tasting it as a Grosse STK site from 1993, a tier that did not then exist; now Falstaff lists a Kranachberg of 1993.
story: the turn to farming without chemicals dated: organic from 2013 in two sources, biodynamic later (respekt-BIODYN from 2021 in one).

others and traps: was Alter Kranachberg a second label beside the Kranachberg; now the name under which Falstaff lists the GSTK from about 2021 (Kranachberg to 2020), since no source shows both in one vintage; sites hedged as the house's description.
open: Whether Ried Alter Kranachberg replaces Ried Kranachberg or sits beside it is not settled: Falstaff lists the plain name to 2020 and Alter from 2021, and a merchant sells a Ried Kranachberg Trinkaus of 2022, a parcel bottling. The record keeps the plan's name and teaches the later one in a trap.
The ridge's height of 400 to 500 metres and its quartz sands rest on the house's sheet alone; a search for a second source found none.

The founding year 1746 is the family's (its site and a profile of 2005); wein.plus gives 1793 as the first written record of winegrowing, so the year stays told as the family's account.

livingNamesMet: Tement: the son who took over in 1976 and his two sons, named in merchant and business pages; the founding couple of 1959 named without dates (the founder died in 1976, his wife's status unknown). None in the fragment.
Sattlerhof: the two brothers who run it and their wives, named in merchant and press pages. None in the fragment.
Gross: the father who ran it from 1984, his two sons and their wives, named in German Wikipedia and wein.plus; the forebear of 1907, Heinrich Gross, named without dates. None in the fragment.
Neumeister: the man who took on the Saziani in 1971 (status unknown), the couple who ran it from 1981 and their son in charge since 2008 or 2009. None in the fragment.
Langmann: no person named in the results read.

swaps.why: the same house and the same wine under the name its label prints: Langmann bottles Schilcher from several Rieden, the Hochgrail among them with its site in the house's pages, Falstaff and two merchants, and the record already teaches it; the key stays. For the read together agent to apply to plan.json.

weighed at the author's invitation: Falstaff lists Alter Kranachberg from about 2021 and the plain name to 2020, but no source says the house dropped the plain label, and a parcel bottling (Ried Kranachberg Trinkaus 2022) still carries the Kranachberg name; the record keeps the plan's name, which holds the site's history from 1993, and teaches the later name in a trap and in others.

codexTension: The region record's producers line calls Sattlerhof's wines among the region's finest and Tement's Zieregg the wine that put the Südsteiermark on the world's lists: judgements the records do not repeat; reported, not edited.

The region record calls Neumeister the Vulkanland's reference and speaks of volcanic soil; the Moarfeitl is limestone sediment over Sarmatian gravel (the house and two merchants); reported, not edited.
The region record calls Langmann the Weststeiermark's Schilcher benchmark, a judgement; reported, not edited.
